context.objective: Document how we carry out Cash Application & Capital Call Receivables, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It starts when the capital call team under FA-01 has released a final capital call notice and set the amount due and due date for each investor, and I'll just walk you through everything from there. First, the assigned tracker owner, who sits on either the CAP Activity Team or the Fund Team, accepts the event handoff, confirms the entity, notice date, due date, bank account and downstream uses, and records the tracker owner and the second reviewer in the cash receivable tracker. Second, the tracker owner loads every investor, expected amount and due date from the final Excel allocation file into the tracker and reconciles the count and total back to the allocation with zero unexplained difference. Third, a few days before the due date, the tracker owner or Investor Services runs the investor portal access report to see who has not accessed the notice, and gives that status to the client. Fourth, the tracker owner or Investor Services sends the reminder emails using the approved template and the CRM contact grid, BCC only, and records the send date in the tracker. Fifth, the tracker owner monitors the bank portal, with Treasury supporting, and captures the value date, amount and originator or reference for each candidate receipt, using the Allvue Audit by Package report where it adds receipt detail. Sixth, the tracker owner matches each receipt to an investor and event in the tracker, or leaves it as unidentified. Seventh, the tracker owner compares cumulative matched receipts to the expected amount and classifies each investor as fully funded, short, overfunded, duplicate, incorrect, missing or unidentified. Eighth, the tracker owner sends the client a funding status report and gets written direction on the exceptions. Ninth, the assigned Fund Team applies the downstream payment gate, comparing cleared cash to management fees, investment funding, line of credit repayment and expenses, and marks each one as cleared to proceed, partially funded or held, and Treasury executes the payments through the FA-17 payment process. Tenth, after the due date the tracker owner keeps following up, calculates days past due using the LPA's business day or calendar day rule, and escalates before any default milestone, with the client directing any legal or default action. Eleventh, the tracker owner and the Fund Team reconcile expected against received, confirm the general ledger and cash balances reflect the actual receipts, update the historical contribution balances, complete client reports such as Cobalt, and lock the final tracker, and the second reviewer verifies the closeout.
What does the second reviewer check during closeout?

They check that the closeout equation holds, meaning the expected receivable equals what was received plus any documented outstanding amount or difference, and that the bank support, the accounting records and the final tracker all agree. We don't mark the event complete while an unidentified or unexplained item is left out of the closeout record. The same reviewer also checks baseline completeness, material matching decisions and exception treatment earlier in the event.
Which role is accountable for the overall result of this work?

I don't know, honestly. The firmwide process owner and the internal approver haven't been confirmed. What I can tell you is that ownership sits with either the CAP Activity Team or the Fund Team and has to be assigned for each event, with one named tracker owner and one second reviewer. The service line governance owner would be the person to confirm who is accountable overall.
How is the event handoff delivered to the assigned tracker owner?

I can't point you to one fixed channel it arrives through, I don't know that there is a set one. What comes over from the FA-01 team is the final allocation schedule, the released notices and the due date, and it gets logged in the event handoff record. If any files, access or ownership are missing, I escalate to the teams responsible for FA-01 and the client account.
What happens when the investor count or total does not reconcile to the final allocation?

I stop and I don't use the tracker. Any mismatch between the notices and the allocation goes back to the FA-01 team to fix, and the baseline has to reconcile to the final allocation before any updates to the tracker begin.
Once FA-01 fixes a mismatch, what tells you the allocation is ready to reconcile again?

I don't know of a specific signal for that. What I can say is that I only work from the locked, final client-approved version of the allocation file from FA-01, so I reconcile again once I have that version, and I check that the investor, entity, event, amount and due date agree between the allocation and the notice.
What happens to a receipt that remains unidentified after the client gives direction?

It stays unassigned and open, I never force a match. I escalate it to the client and Treasury, keep it in the unidentified cash log with the research, and keep refreshing the transaction detail or getting Treasury, bank or remittance support. Until it is supported, that cash can't satisfy an investor's receivable or fund a downstream payment, and at closeout it has to be shown explicitly as unidentified in the closeout record.
What information do you compare to match a bank receipt to an investor and capital-call event?

I compare the receipt amount, the originator or reference, the value date and the custodian information against the expected investors in the tracker. Where several investors pay through a shared custodian, I use the amount and the remaining unmatched investor list as support, and process of elimination is only a documented last resort. I never match on the originator name alone, and if the evidence is insufficient I contact the approved party for more remittance detail.
When a receipt is identified as short, overfunded, duplicate or incorrect, what happens to resolve it?
This capture still has open sections. 13 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

notes.summary: Receipt matching uses amount, reference, value date and custodian information. Shared-custodian payments may require a documented last-resort elimination; insufficient evidence prompts a request for remittance detail.

topics.answer: The intake calls the work Cash Application & Capital Call Receivables. It covers tracking expected capital-call receipts through funding status and closeout; other names and precise boundaries are UNKNOWN.

The work produces investor funding status, payment funding classifications and reconciled closeout records, including a locked tracker. The participant's own statement of the overall delivered result and downstream uses is UNKNOWN.

FA-01 releases a final capital call notice and sets each investor's amount and due date; the assigned tracker owner accepts the handoff. The handoff includes notices, allocation and due date, but its channel is not fixed or known. Access reporting occurs a few days before the due date; follow-up continues after it and escalation occurs before any default milestone. Event frequency and other fixed deadlines are UNKNOWN.

Closeout includes reconciliation, ledger and cash confirmation, historical balance updates, client reports, a locked tracker and second-reviewer verification. Expected receivables must equal receipts plus documented outstanding amounts or differences, and bank support, accounting records and tracker must agree. Unidentified or unexplained items cannot be omitted from the closeout record; unidentified cash must be shown explicitly. Who marks completion, how it is recorded and downstream consumers are UNKNOWN.

Event ownership is assigned to either the CAP Activity Team or Fund Team, with a named tracker owner and second reviewer. Firmwide process ownership and internal approval are unconfirmed; the participant identified the service line governance owner as the person to confirm overall accountability.

The tracker owner accepts the handoff, records assignments, loads and reconciles the allocation, and, with Investor Services as an alternative performer, reports notice access and sends reminders. The owner monitors receipts with Treasury support, matches or leaves them unidentified, classifies funding and obtains client direction. The Fund Team applies a cash gate and Treasury executes payments through FA-17. After the due date the owner follows up and escalates before default milestones; the owner and Fund Team perform closeout and a second reviewer verifies it. Mismatches return to FA-01; insufficient or unidentified receipt evidence is pursued separately. Several exception exits, review placements and handoff mechanisms remain UNKNOWN.

The owner reconciles baseline count and total, checks specified notice fields and uses multiple receipt details for matching. Reminders use the approved template and CRM grid, BCC only. The second reviewer checks baseline completeness, material matches and exception treatment earlier, then the closeout equation and agreement of bank support, accounting records and tracker. The client supplies written exception direction; the Fund Team applies a payment gate. Review timing, failure rework, retained proof, thresholds, segregation, overrides and system enforcement are UNKNOWN.

Shared-custodian receipts use amount and the remaining unmatched investor list as support, with documented elimination only as a last resort. Unidentified receipts require research and remain open while unsupported. Whether these circumstances change the process boundary, and their effort or other constraints, is UNKNOWN.
